content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Lists** as part of **Strings, Arrays, and Collections**. A list models ordered elements; distinguish read-only views from mutable collections and select operations based on required ordering and complexity. Use the subtopics—Creating Lists, Accessing, Searching, and Updating Elements, List Sorting and Slicing—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Functions, null safety, strings, and collections are the building blocks of most practical Kotlin code. Choosing the right operation reduces avoidable errors and makes behavior easier to test.
